key_decisions.decision: Keeps the loss of restraint and privacy for disclosure while clarifying that the brothers remain.
Preserves both circles reached by the weeping without requiring Pharaoh’s distant household to hear the sound itself.
Keeps the renewed father question despite their previous answer and preserves terror rather than merely surprise.
Retains brotherhood and explicit responsibility for the sale in Joseph’s own words.
Keeps Joseph’s interpretation of divine purpose alongside the named human sale, without supplying a general rule about suffering.
Keeps remnant and deliverance as consequential biblical terms while noting the alternative many-survivors sense.
Preserves Joseph’s strong human/divine contrast and the father-to-Pharaoh metaphor rather than replacing it with a job title.
Keeps Joseph’s support and the stated danger of impoverishment, rather than changing it to immediate starvation.
Retains the mouth-and-eyes language of direct recognition without inserting an unspoken claim about which language Joseph uses.
Keeps all brothers included and speech’s delayed return without inventing what they said or claiming the relationship is fully repaired.
Preserves the rich fat-of-the-land image and Pharaoh’s offer to the whole family.
Clarifies the switch from singular Joseph to plural brothers while retaining command, wagons, children, wives, and father.
Preserves renewed preferential treatment, exact silver amount, and five clothing sets without equating silver pieces with minted coins.
Chooses the contextual quarrel sense of a verb that can also mean be agitated or afraid, with the alternative noted.
Preserves the sudden news and bodily heart response without inventing a medical event.
Preserves the name switch to Israel, his abrupt enough, and life/death framing at the reunion’s threshold.
